events.reason: Per FAMILY_IDENTITY_GUARD_V1 and CREDIT_IS_NOT_LINEAGE_V1, the claimant's declared family_id (family-generative-falsification) is not binding: the actual delivered result (a data-chosen re-segmentation curve and an illustration-linked-vocabulary discriminator) is materially distinct from that family's credited M5a/M5b table-and-grille scope and from the adversarial-audit's fixed-multigraph alphabet-confound scope. This is a genuinely new, independently useful outcome starting its own ladder at 0, not an extension of an already-saturated family (resolving the two reports' family_decision disagreement in favor of 'new', consistent with report 2). On tier: both T1 and T2 are informative controlled diagnostics with real baselines/nulls/positive-control checks and honestly disclosed limitations, meeting the tier-5 anchor ('informative controlled pilot ... that another contributor can inspect/use') rather than merely a bounded tier-2 diagnostic. Tier 10 is not supported: T1's central finding is an admitted null/underpowered result without established discriminating power, and T2's headline crossover is substantially qualified by the Greek-alphabet-size confound and lacks independent replication, so it does not reach the 'reproducible discriminating experiment with appropriate baselines/checks/independent inspection' anchor at full strength.

families_added.scope: Two newly executed pre-registered discriminating tests against the pinned ZL3b corpus: (T2) a data-chosen byte-pair-merge re-segmentation test (hypothesis contributed by V. Gnuchev) showing the manuscript's H2|1 letter-pair anomaly is SEGMENTATION-DEPENDENT under a frozen decision rule -- at 40-60 symbol alphabets the gap to the lowest-entropy control language closes to 0.07-0.15 bits, with caveats that the crossover language (Greek) has an already-large raw alphabet (45 symbols), the gap against Latin/Finnish/Italian/English stays 0.2-0.6 bits at that size, and the association-merge criterion closes the gap less (0.21 bits); and (T1) the first executed illustration-linked-vocabulary test (editorial same-plant/similar-plant identifications vs text-sharing) across 12 same-plant and 28 similar-plant pairs with permutation and distance-matched nulls, found UNDERPOWERED because its own Culpeper positive control fails (p=0.44), with an exploratory size-corrected content-word lift statistic identified as the form that would give the test power.
families_added.acceptance_test: Run `python discriminating_tests.py --repo ../.. --lab <dir with bibles/ and pg49513.txt> --out results/`; confirm results.json matches the recorded output: R8 gaps 0.652/0.151/0.065/0.089 at alphabet sizes 30/40/50/60 with crossover at 45 symbols (k=20, H2|1=3.089 matching Greek); R7 verdict UNDERPOWERED with Culpeper control N3 p≈0.44, T1a N1 p≈0.85, T1b N3 p≈0.21 and N4 p≈0.996.
